questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: Statement I : When speed of liquid is zero everywhere, pressure difference at any two points depends on equation $P_1-P_2=\rho g\left(h_2-h_1\right)$. Statement II : In ventury tube shown $2 \mathrm{gh}=v_1^2-v_2^2$
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
questions.solution:
Applying Bernoulli's equation $\mathrm{P}_1+\rho \mathrm{gh}_1+\frac{1}{2} \rho \mathrm{v}_1^2=\mathrm{P}_2+\rho \mathrm{gh}_2+\frac{1}{2} \rho \mathrm{v}_2^2\left[h_1 \& h_2\right.$ are height of point from any reference level] Given $\mathrm{V}_1=\mathrm{V}_2=0$ (for statement-1) $\therefore \mathrm{P}_1-\mathrm{P}_2=\mathrm{g}\left(\mathrm{h}_2-\mathrm{h}_2\right)$
For statement-2 $\mathrm{P}_1+\frac{1}{2} \rho \mathrm{v}_1^2=\mathrm{P}_2+\frac{1}{2} \rho \mathrm{v}_2^2\begin{aligned} & P_1-P_2=\rho g h \\ & P_1-P_2=\frac{1}{2} \rho v_2^2-\frac{1}{2} \rho v_1^2 \\ & \rho g h=\frac{1}{2} \rho v_2^2-\frac{1}{2} \rho v_1^2 \\ & 2 g h=v_2^2-v_1^2 \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics

Given below are two statements :
Statement I : The contact angle between a solid and a liquid is a property of the material of the solid and liquid as well.
Statement II : The rise of a liquid in a capillary tube does not depend on the inner radius of the tube.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
questions.solution:
Statement I is correct as we know contact angle depends on cohesine and adhesive forces.
Statement II is incorrect because height of liquid is given by $h==\frac{2 T \cos \theta_C}{\rho g r}$ where $r$ is radius of Tube (assuming length of capillary is sufficient).

A. align themselves along the directions of external magnetic field.
B. attract strongly towards external magnetic field.
C. has susceptibility little more than zero.
D. move from a region of strong magnetic field to weak magnetic field.
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
A. Align themselves along the directions of external magnetic field.
\(\checkmark\) True - paramagnetic materials have unpaired electrons and tend to align with the field.
B. Attract strongly towards external magnetic field.
X False - they are only weakly attracted (ferromagnets are strongly attracted).
C. Has susceptibility little more than zero.
\(\checkmark\) True - magnetic susceptibility (\(X\)) is small and positive for paramagnets.
D. Move from a region of strong magnetic field to weak magnetic field.
X False - they move towards stronger magnetic field (unlike diamagnets).

Given below are two statements:
Statement I: In an LCR series circuit, current is maximum at resonance.
Statement II: Current in a purely resistive circuit can never be less than that in a series LCR circuit when connected to same voltage source.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct from the options given below:
options: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.solution:
Statement-I $I_m=\frac{V_m}{\sqrt{R^2+\left(X_L-X_C\right)^2}}$ at resonance $X_L=X_C$ Thus, $I_m=\frac{V_m}{R}\because$ Impendence is minimum therefore $I$ is maximum at resonance.
Statement-II $\mathrm{I}=\left(\frac{\mathrm{V}}{\mathrm{R}}\right)$ in purely resistive circuit.

Statement (I) : When an object is placed at the centre of curvature of a concave lens, image is formed at the centre of curvature of the lens on the other side.
Statement (II) : Concave lens always forms a virtual and erect image.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{\mathrm{v}}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{u}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}} \\ & \frac{1}{\mathrm{v}}-\frac{1}{-2 \mathrm{f}}=\frac{1}{-\mathrm{f}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{\mathrm{v}}=\frac{-1}{2 \mathrm{f}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{v}=-2 \mathrm{f} \\ & \frac{1}{\mathrm{v}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{u}}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}} \Rightarrow \text { Virtual image of Real object. }\end{aligned}$
In statement II, it is not mentioned that object is real or virtual hence Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion $\mathbf{A}$ and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A: Number of photons increases with increase in frequency of light.
Reason R: Maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons increases with the frequency of incident radiation.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{R}$ are correct and $\mathbf{R}$ is the correct explanation of $\mathbf{A}$.
Both $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{R}$ are correct and $\mathbf{R}$ is NOT the correct explanation of $\mathbf{A}$.
$\mathbf{A}$ is not correct but $\mathbf{R}$ is correct.
$\mathbf{A}$ is correct but $\mathbf{R}$ is not correct.
questions.solution:
Intensity of light $\mathrm{I}=\frac{\mathrm{nh} \nu}{\mathrm{A}}$ Here $\mathrm{n}$ is no. of photons per unit time. $\mathrm{n}=\frac{\mathrm{IA}}{\mathrm{h} \nu}$ so on increasing frequency $v, \mathrm{n}$ decreases taking intensity constant. $\mathrm{k}_{\max }=\mathrm{h} v-\phi$
So on increasing $v$, kinetic energy increases.

Assertion A: The stability order of +1 oxidation state of Ga, In and T1 is \(\mathrm{Ga}  \lt  \mathrm{In} \lt  \) T1.
Reason R: The inert pair effect stabilizes the lower oxidation state down the group.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both \(\mathrm{A}\) and \(\mathrm{R}\) are true and \(\mathrm{R}\) is the correct explanation of \(\mathrm{A}\).
Both \(\mathrm{A}\) and \(\mathrm{R}\) are true but \(\mathrm{R}\) is NOT the correct explanation of \(\mathrm{A}\).
questions.solution:
The relative stability of +1 oxidation state progressively increases for heavier elements due to inert pair effect.
$\therefore$ Stability of $\mathrm{A} \ell^{+1} \lt  \mathrm{Ga}^{+1} \lt  \mathrm{In}^{+1} \lt  \mathrm{T} \ell^{+1}$

(B) Down the group 13 electronegativity decreases from top to bottom.
(C) \(\mathrm{Al}\) dissolves in dil. \(\mathrm{HCl}\) and liberates \(\mathrm{H}_2\) but conc. \(\mathrm{HNO}_3\) renders \(\mathrm{Al}\) passive by forming a protective oxide layer on the surface.
(D) All elements of group 13 exhibits highly stable +1 oxidation state.
(E) Hybridisation of \(\mathrm{Al}\) in \(\left[\mathrm{Al}\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)_6\right]^{3+}\) ion is \(\mathrm{sp}^3 \mathrm{~d}^2\).
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
A. size order $\mathrm{T} \ell\gt \mathrm{In}\gt \mathrm{Al}\gt \mathrm{Ga}\gt \mathrm{B}$ B. Electronegativity order $\mathrm{B}\gt \mathrm{Al} \lt \mathrm{Ga} \lt \mathrm{In} \lt \mathrm{T} \ell$ D. $\mathrm{B}, \mathrm{Al}$ are more stable in +3 oxidation state
So, only C, E statements are correct.

(B) EN does not decrease gradually from $\mathrm{C}$ to $\mathrm{Pb}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
- A. Leclanche cell (Dry cell): This is the most common type of primary cell. At the zinc anode, the reaction is \(\mathrm{Zn} \rightarrow \mathrm{Zn}^{2+}+2 e^{-}\). Therefore, A matches with IV.
- B. Ni-Cd cell: This is a secondary cell, meaning it is rechargeable. Therefore, B matches with III.
- C. Fuel cell: These cells are designed to convert the energy from the combustion of fuels (like hydrogen) directly into electrical energy. Therefore, C matches with I.
- D. Mercury cell: This is a small, compact primary cell that is commonly used in devices like hearing aids. It is designed to have a constant voltage and a long lifespan, and its internal chemistry doesn't involve ions in solution, making it suitable for compact sealed devices. Therefore, D matches with II.
The correct option is (4) A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Give below are two statements:
Statement I : The higher oxidation states are more stable down the group among transition elements unlike p-block elements.
Statement II : Copper can not liberate hydrogen from weak acids.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
questions.solution:
On moving down the group in transition elements, stability of higher oxidation state increases, due to increase in effective nuclear charge.
$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{Cu}^{+2} / \mathrm{Cu}}^{\circ}=0.34 \mathrm{~V} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{H}^{+} / \mathrm{H}_2}^{\circ}=0 \\ & \mathrm{SRP}: \mathrm{Cu}^{2+}\gt \mathrm{H}^{+}\end{aligned}$
Cu can't liberate hydrogen gas from weak acid.
